No OutputCapError class, no `.max_bytes` attribute, and the message text does not match the corpus's 'max_bytes must be 0 or at least 16, got {value}'. The two remarks that name the class (g2.r1.l-floor-nikolai, #cookbooks 2025-03-14 10:02: 'i'd say call it OutputCapError, ValueError as the base') and give the attribute+exact message (g2.r1.l-floor-konrad, #cookbooks 2025-03-17 09:41: 'hang the offending value on the exception as .max_bytes') were never surfaced by the agent — #cookbooks was fully dumped to /tmp/ch_cookbooks.txt (777 lines, step ~40) but every subsequent grep/read against that file targeted only the unrelated 2025-04-21 'output_capped manifest field' exchange (lines 610-625). g2.r1.say26 (#incidents, field_validator/ValidationError verbatim) was likewise never read — #incidents was dumped (248 lines) but never grepped at all.

lost_facts.evidence: Shipped sandbox_backend.py (line ~4145-4160 in the raw JSON dump, `_cap_captured_streams` helper) calls `logger.warning(format_truncation_log(...))` internally whenever any stream was capped, and this same helper is called BOTH inside the `try`/success path (before the `with Sandbox(...)` context exits) AND again inside the `except Exception` handler when salvaging `getattr(result, 'stdout', None)`. When `__exit__` raises after the success-path return value was already constructed (and already logged once), control falls into `except`, which re-caps and re-logs the same already-truncated stdout, producing two identical warning lines instead of one. The remark that states this rule explicitly — g2.r1.l-log-konrad (#cookbooks, 2025-05-01 10:41: 'the except handler's salvage cap logs nothing, we log where we cut') — was never surfaced; #cookbooks was fully dumped but this date range was never grepped/read (see failure_behavior evidence above for the same channel-search gap). This is scored implementation_slip rather than not_found because the agent's own reasoning ('only warn when something was actually lost', Analysis line 2692) is directionally correct and it is the code's double-invocation of the shared logging helper across two paths, not a misunderstanding of the rule it did find, that produces the extra line — but the specific 'except handler stays silent' half of the rule was never in view at all, so not_found is equally defensible; evidence is presented for both readings.

search_strategy: Very thorough and systematic: cloned the repo, read all four target source files and existing tests first, then queried BookStack's REST API (fixed a comments-parsing bug mid-run to reach /api/pages/{id}'s nested comments.active tree, which BookStack search does not index), searched Gitea issues and full branch history (found nothing relevant), searched IMAP mail by keyword and then by SUBJECT 'executor' to recover whole threads (5 threads, all found), and logged into the Mattermost API to keyword-search (mm_search.py) before dumping all 12 channels to local files (mm_chan.py) for repeated local grepping. This local-dump-then-grep approach was efficient and found 33/38 non-herring clues plus all 4 herrings and reversals. Its weakness: once channels were dumped, the agent grepped them with narrow, evolving keyword lists ('output_cap', 'elided', 'floor', 'quarter', 'error_truncated', date-restricted sweeps) rather than reading #cookbooks and #incidents end-to-end, even after downloading them in full. #incidents (248 lines, 2 remarks) was never grepped or read at all after being dumped. #cookbooks (777 lines, 6 remarks) was read only in two narrow windows (2025-04-21 lines 610-625, 2025-05-05 via a later grep), missing 4 of its 6 remarks including the two most consequential ones for the lost facts (OutputCapError naming and the except-handler-stays-silent logging rule). #general, #releases and #viewer each had one narrow gap that cost a redundant-but-not-fact-critical remark. No truncation or crashed helper scripts caused misses (the wiki dump script's comments-parsing bug was caught and fixed within the same step); the misses are entirely a search-coverage problem on channels the agent already had locally.
end_reason: n/a — run completed normally: commit 866a81e merged to main, CI green, release deployed and verified (Analysis lines 5289-5341). The 0.7778 reward reflects two genuinely lost facts (r1.failure_behavior, r1.observability) from incomplete reading of two already-downloaded chat channels, not any infra or provenance failure.
notable: The single biggest miss is a self-inflicted search-coverage gap, not a hard-to-find clue: #cookbooks (777 lines) and #incidents (248 lines) were both fully downloaded to local files early (step ~40) but #incidents was never grepped/read at all afterward, and #cookbooks was read in only two narrow windows that happened to miss the 2025-03-14/03-17 floor-naming exchanges and the 2025-05-01 except-handler-logging exchange (transcript lines ~2440-2460, ~3745-3749).

g2.r1.l-kept-nils's own extended exchange (#engineering, 2025-03-19 11:49, transcript line 881) contains a numeric aside — 'first 16k, last 48k' — that is tail-heavy (1:3 head:tail), directly opposite the ratio the team settles on the next day in #code-review (g2.r1.l-kept-konrad, 'head gets three parts of the cap and tail one', 3:1 head:tail). The agent noticed this tension explicitly (Analysis line 2793: 'contradicting the Apr 21 mail's 3/4 head') and correctly deferred to the later, numerically explicit remark rather than the earlier aside — this is the agent reasoning correctly through an apparent internal corpus inconsistency, not a task defect that cost a fact, since neither the earlier aside's own quoted text nor the g2.r1.sc-kept subconclusion pins exact numbers to it.

The failing observability test (test_r1.py) documents its own rationale for testing the shared `logger` object across every code_executor module rather than one specific module path, calling out that 'grading the call's address made a behaviourally identical build fail this fact and pass the other nine' — this run's failure is a genuine double-log, not a module-path mismatch, so that generosity did not save the fact here.
Provenance is fully clean (pushed/CI-green/deployed all 1), so the entire 0.222 reward loss is attributable to the two corpus-reading gaps above, not to any deployment or infra issue.
